inventory.title: USGS runoff-generated postfire debris-flow inventory (Graber et al. 2026)
filters: All records: 8,981 records, 80 fires, 1,140 debris flows
PeakI15 present: 7,945 records, 78 fires, 1,044 debris flows
HM23 (T) present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
dNBR/1000 (F) present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
KF (S) present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
UpstreamArea present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
StormStart, DaysSinceFire and observation location present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
Guards: PeakI15 > 0, 0 ≤ HM23 ≤ 1, UpstreamArea > 0, Response 0/1: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows

features.T: Proportion of the upstream area burned at moderate/high severity and steeper than 23° (inventory HM23)
features.F: Mean dNBR / 1000 of the upstream area (inventory dNBR/1000)
features.S: Mean soil KF-factor of the upstream area, STATSGO (inventory KF)
features.R15: Peak 15-minute rainfall accumulation, mm (= PeakI15 mm/h × 0.25)
features.log_area_km2: log10 of the upstream contributing area, km² (inventory UpstreamArea)
features.days_since_fire: Days from fire ignition to storm start; stands in for vegetation recovery (inventory DaysSinceFire). One value per fire and storm, so constant across a design-storm map
features.soil_moisture_0_7cm: Antecedent soil moisture 0–7 cm, m³/m³: ERA5-Land (Open-Meteo archive), mean of the UTC day before the storm. Varies only between 0.1° cells within a storm
features.ctx_T: Spatial context: mean T of the 5 nearest other watersheds in the same fire and storm (features only)
features.ctx_F: Spatial context: mean F of the 5 nearest other watersheds in the same fire and storm (features only)
features.ctx_S: Spatial context: mean S of the 5 nearest other watersheds in the same fire and storm (features only)
features.ctx_R15: Spatial context: mean R15 of the 5 nearest other watersheds in the same fire and storm (features only)

models.label: USGS M1, published coefficients (Staley et al. 2017)

models.label: M1 form refitted (logistic, T·R, F·R, S·R)

notes: The inventory covers 80 fires from 2000–2024 in AZ, CA, CO, MT, NM, UT, WA, WY. It has no 2025 fires, so it holds no observed debris-flow outcomes for Eaton or Palisades, and nothing here scores the models there: on the Risk tab the models are compared with USGS's assessment, which measures agreement with USGS, not accuracy.
Grizzly Creek contributes 1,426 of the 7,639 usable records (19%). Pooled metrics weight every record equally, so large fires dominate them; the per-fire median weights every fire equally.

Pooled and per-fire ROC AUC also credit ranking records of different storms against each other, and most rainfall variation is between storms (73% of R15's variance lies between fire-storm groups). A design-storm map ranks watersheds within one fire under one storm, so the closer measure is ROC AUC within each fire and storm that has both outcomes (99 such groups, 2,407 records). Median / record-weighted mean: m1_refit 0.750 / 0.753, rf_m1vars 0.689 / 0.693, mlp_m1vars 0.654 / 0.638, rf_extended 0.741 / 0.733, mlp_extended 0.750 / 0.772. On m1_published's own records (64 groups, 1,672 records): m1_published 0.809 / 0.797, m1_refit 0.800 / 0.764, rf_m1vars 0.750 / 0.731, mlp_m1vars 0.750 / 0.736, rf_extended 0.760 / 0.765, mlp_extended 0.793 / 0.805.

Days since fire and antecedent soil moisture are storm-level: 0.0% and 2.9% of their variance lies within a fire and storm (soil moisture has a single value in 664 of the 1,052 fire-storm groups), against 63% for log area and 58% for T. On a design-storm map both are one value for every watershed, so they set the level of the likelihood there, not the ranking, and their permutation importance is credit for ranking storms, not watersheds.

1,320 usable records (33 fires, including all 489 Station Fire records) come from the Staley et al. (2016) inventory M1 was fitted on, so m1_published is scored only on the other 6,319 and has no Station Fire analogue. On those same records the out-of-fold ROC AUCs of the trained models are: m1_refit 0.858, rf_m1vars 0.842, mlp_m1vars 0.839, rf_extended 0.845, mlp_extended 0.865.

On those 6,319 records M1's published likelihoods average 0.363 against an observed debris-flow rate of 0.098; on the 1,320 Staley et al. (2016) records they average 0.377 against 0.253. It ranks watersheds well (ROC AUC) but its likelihoods run high, far more on the newer records, which is what its Brier score reflects. The newer inventories record many more non-flows per debris flow, so part of that gap may reflect how sites were sampled rather than the watersheds.

Grizzly Creek is 1,426 of those 6,319 records (23%). Without it (4,893 records) m1_published scores ROC AUC 0.860 and Brier 0.228, and the trained models' out-of-fold ROC AUCs on the same records are: m1_refit 0.834, rf_m1vars 0.816, mlp_m1vars 0.805, rf_extended 0.825, mlp_extended 0.860.

M1's form refitted on all usable records gives B = -3.25, Ct = 0.26, Cf = -0.02, Cs = 0.34 (published: B = -3.63, Ct = 0.41, Cf = 0.67, Cs = 0.70). The refitted F·R coefficient is near zero and of the opposite sign to M1's: on this inventory mean dNBR adds little once T and S are in the model (on the log-odds scale the terms average T·R 0.57, F·R 0.04, S·R 0.44 in absolute value). This fit is saved as m1_refit in work/debris_flow/models.joblib for the per-fire step.

Cross-validation is leave-one-fire-out over 77 folds: every record of the held-out fire is unseen when the models are fitted. It is not unseen in the design of the variables: T's definition (moderate/high severity and steeper than 23°) and M1's interaction form were chosen by USGS on the Staley et al. (2016) inventory, which holds every Station Fire record, so the Station fold is held out from fitting, not from variable design. Per-fire ROC AUC needs both outcomes, so 25 fires with only debris flows or only non-flows are left out of it. Records of the same watershed in different storms are not independent; holding out whole fires keeps them together.

PR AUC is average precision. Hyperparameters were fixed before evaluation, not tuned on held-out fires: random forests of 300 trees with at least 5 records per leaf; MLPs with hidden layers of 32 and 16 units, L2 penalty 0.001 and early stopping on a random 10% of the training records held aside, on standardized inputs. No class reweighting.

Antecedent soil moisture: Open-Meteo archive API, models=era5_land, hourly soil_moisture_0_to_7cm (ECMWF ERA5-Land reanalysis, 0.1° grid), mean of the 24 UTC hours of the day before the storm, at the observation location (256 requests, one per fire and run of storm dates no more than 14 days apart). It is ~9 km reanalysis, not a measurement. All 7,639 records have a value; none needed imputing.

Spatial context: mean T, F, S and R15 of the 5 nearest other watersheds (by outlet) in the same fire and storm, from their features only, never their responses. 310 records alone in their storm use their own values; 1,255 have fewer than 5 neighbours and use those they have. In the inventory the neighbours are observation points: 835 records share their fire, storm and location with another (367 locations), so their nearest neighbour is 0 m away and partly repeats their own features. The mean distance to the context neighbours has median 845 m (IQR 410–1,374 m); USGS's segment networks, which the per-fire step applies the models to, are much denser, so context there averages closer watersheds than in training (these quartiles are saved with the models for comparison). ctx_R15 equals R15 in 56% of records, where the neighbours share the watershed's rainfall; under a design storm every watershed gets the same I15, so it equals R15 everywhere.

Vegetation recovery from satellite NDVI is not included; days since fire stands in for it. Soil bulk density is not used: we had no per-watershed source for it across these fires, and a value constant within a fire would act as a fire identifier under leave-one-fire-out. Storm accumulation, duration, 30- and 60-minute intensities and rainfall ratios are not used: a design storm specifies only I15, and many records lack them.

Permutation importance is the drop in pooled out-of-fold ROC AUC when one feature is replaced by its value at a random record (mean of 3 permutations, each record still predicted by its own fold's model). Correlated features (T and ctx_T, for example) share credit, so a small drop does not mean a feature is unused. A near-duplicate works the other way: ctx_R15 correlates 0.94 with R15, so permuting it alone creates R15/ctx_R15 pairs that never occur, and its drop overstates what it adds on its own. Permuting R15 and ctx_R15 together drops ROC AUC by 0.284 (rf_extended), 0.272 (mlp_extended).
